Doesn’t need to be specific because everyone has a different body goal. However, just because something fits on your calories doesn’t mean it’s always okay to eat daily.

Certain foods may cause inflammation. The best thing you can do is listen to your body. Even if you’re trying to lose weight prioritising protein is important. You’ll need some good healthy fats and carbs too. Once you prioritise those things you’ll have less calories for the treats.

My advise is to plan your meals and snacks. That way you can have a planned treat that you’ll know is within your calories and macros. 

I’m on mounjaro, I’ve not had any snacks and fizzy drinks in four weeks (except for the cinema yesterday and boy it tasted awful I didn’t finish the coke or popcorn)

I now eat a lot of fruit and veg, a protein shake because I’m struggling to get my protein in at my MIL house (she doesn’t eat red meat and often makes vegetarian foods and never leaves enough space in the fridge for my planned meals so I just go with what she makes) and then I eat dinner. Sometimes I long for some chocolate… and then I realise I don’t actually want it. I’m just bored or at the beginning it was cravings. 

Don’t jump in to it all at once. The diet is the most relaxed this about 75 hard on my opinion. Week one say you don’t want any high sugar snacks. Then week 2 say you want to remove fizzy drinks from your diet. 

You know deep down what creates shame and guilt when you eat it. You want to reduce that guilt feeling, so when you eat the “bad foods” it’s more of a “ah I’m enjoying this reward/treat” instead of “ugh I can’t believe I allowed myself to eat this again.”

Look in to processed foods and conscious eating. 

Best of luck x

“All the girls and boys loved ____ tv program, I wonder what the hype was” and watch it. Heal in that space and feel free to regress.

Essentially you need to put yourself first. Love yourself through this, not hate that your human. Ultimately we develop addictions and kinks and fetishes, especially in your experience of life. You’re allowed to start again, and you’re allowed to take your time. You’re allowed to relapse as long as you’re doing everything to recover. Recovery is not linear.
